## Magazine requirements and evolution

The first magazine request was a PDF in `bestiary/`, styled after 1990s Nintendo Power and GamePro, with monster
history/description, hyperrealistic portrait and in-game pictures attacking the heroes. History was to come from
Storyboarding. The user subsequently moved marketing output into `marketing/`.

The user added Tony and Sean before monsters, with backstory explicitly TODO until Storyboarding supplied it.
The cover must show both together against a horde of regular monsters, not bosses. Bosses belong inside the magazine.
BJ belongs after the heroes and before the monsters. BJ needed a distinctive, memorable AI identity, with the existing
Bestiary / Art agent responsible for artwork. Old sci-fi AI and Portal were examples of recognizability, not requests
to copy their designs.

Early random-stance material called From Portrait to Pixels was rejected in favor of actual monster sprite sheets.
Later, the user rejected the overall sprawling design: two or three pages per creature was too much. The new direction
was compact groupings with short blurbs and one or two pictures, perhaps only one or two selected sheet pages for
interest. This later request supersedes any assumption that every creature must retain a full-sheet spread.
Missing Clogfather portrait/sprite and a duplicated flying-spider ending were specifically called out for correction.

Eleven magazine reference images supplied examples of bold colored bands, condensed columns, oversized shadowed type,
bordered screenshots, character cutouts, asymmetric grouping and dense but readable pages. Edition 17 condensed the
seventeen-page design into eight pages. The current sequence is cover; paired crew profiles; BJ/dispenser; first
creature roundup; second creature roundup; gameplay feature; curated action gallery; company advertisement.
Page 4 groups Flushfiend and Hallowed Widow; page 5 groups Clogfather and Septic Air Force. The action gallery is not a
promise that every depicted source pose is validated game animation.

## Editorial corrections and non-negotiable preferences

The user supplied the Avoid Formulaic AI Copy section for AGENTS.md and asked that it be read before regeneration.
It rejects repetitive paired fragments such as Two plumbers. One impossible job.; No tools. No backup. No problem.;
and Teeth in the bathroom. Wings in the basement. Favor natural varied sentence lengths, complete sentences when
appropriate, specific observations and distinctive voice. Paired fragments are rare exceptions, not a default formula.
Review creative prose for repeated rhetorical patterns before delivery. The exact section is preserved in the source
appendix. Edition 18 examples include MIND THE FIXTURES! and a crew introduction about Tony teaching Sean a trade that
keeps getting stranger. A later explicitly approved headline remains approved even if it resembles a general pattern.

The intended editorial voice is an experienced plumbing trade editor: warm toward the crew, dry toward management,
concrete and conversational. Use Tony and Sean only, never surnames. Tony is the experienced, patient plumber; Sean is
his inexperienced apprentice. Keep future outcomes and internal story proposals out of promotional canon.

Remove production talk throughout publication, including captions, contents, metadata, headings and sidebars.
Do not mention the viewer's screen. Do not print runtime integration, frame counts, atlas terminology, collision
details,
agent discussions or build IDs. Player terms such as health, attacks, checkpoint and reload can be useful.
The user explicitly rejected Shown in an earlier version of the game and Widow preview artwork — an encounter idea
we are exploring. Do not replace those with synonymous tentative disclaimers. Captions may describe subject, action,
atmosphere or useful player information. Preserve provenance internally, and do not imply planned encounters playable.

A real unresolved editorial TODO must read `TODO: <specific missing item>` in a large bold high-contrast box, at least
18 pt and unclipped. No small italic caveats. Existing art does not need a TODO solely because implementation is
pending.
Remove fictional-company, fictional-publication and non-affiliation notices from the reader edition. This was an
explicit
user correction, including the phrase Fictional Company Notice. Keep factual internal metadata separate.

Preserve old artwork/source versions unless the user specifically directs deletion. Do not paint over obsolete text
inside authentic game screenshots to pretend they are current. Ask the existing Art agent for new artwork rather than
independently generating replacement assets. Avoid future plot spoilers, origin explanations and boss solutions.

## Employee dispenser: feedback, approved tone and assets

The user rejected explicit prose describing the dispenser grabbing and crumpling a hero and throwing the result at the
viewer. The machine does kill heroes in the fiction, but the magazine must suggest a disturbing corporate practice
through euphemism and omission. Both paragraphs needed this treatment; merely softening the first was insufficient.
The user requested new text from Storyboarding and new artwork from Art, while explicitly holding magazine regeneration
until later. Subsequent authorization produced edition 19.

The rusty old-box appearance was liked, but it did not read as a vending machine. The requested redesign adds a glass
front with a couple of sleeping clones of the current hero for dispensing. Art was asked for sleeping Tony/Sean sprites
and an updated cabinet. Original marketing artwork shows two copies of the matching hero per variant. Later runtime
records describe a one-spare cabinet; do not silently rewrite the archived magazine's original design as if it always
had one occupant. Magazine integration and runtime delivery are separate states.

Storyboarding supplied feature copy about Mainframe making arrangements, familiar occupants, reserve personnel,
respecting their rest, continuity of service, assignments/tools/name on the rota and a leaflet referring questions back
to itself. The selected caption asks that reserve personnel not be disturbed. The exact handoff is in the appendix.
Its proposed replacement headlines/advertisement were not all selected. In particular, preserve the user-praised ad:
WE VALUE OUR STAFF. THAT IS WHY WE KEEP SPARES. Keep PLEASE COLLECT YOUR REPLACEMENT for the feature rather than
assuming
a proposed Mainframe has made arrangements headline was accepted. The back footer now names the dispenser and says
Your name is already on the schedule. Historical preview disclaimers in the copy handoff are superseded.

Assets are `marketing/spare-employee-dispenser/tony-stocked-v1.png` and `sean-stocked-v1.png`, transparent 1024×1536
marketing cutouts. They depict rusty teal/brass, glass, coin strip and dispensing hatch without gore. They are flattened
marketing illustrations, not layered game sprites. Exact prompts are in `glass-front-prompts-v1.json` in that folder.
Feature page uses Tony; back advertisement uses Sean. Notes judged them usable at approximately 150 pt; a future
full-page 300 dpi print requirement needs another art pass rather than an unsupported quality claim.
Sleeping hero sources include `assets/world/spare-employee-dispenser/sleeping-heroes-v1.png`, `sleeping-heroes-v2.png`
and `sleeping-heroes-v2.json`; the revised sheet is recorded as 1536×1024.

## Explicit game feature raised during magazine review

The user noticed the dark area below a platform in a gameplay picture and asked whether it was water. They then
explicitly requested flowing wastewater along the bottom of the first level, represented as a cutaway/x-ray view into
a large pipe under the floor. Random debris and things that should never have been flushed float past. As the player
approaches Clogfather, water level drops and debris increases. At the boss, no water flows and the pipe is completely
blocked with grease/oil/disgusting debris. Preserve this requested progression rather than replacing it with a different
hydraulic interpretation. The user authorized coordination with Storyboarding, Level Design, Art and Engineering.

Marketing coordinated those disciplines and handed off implementation. Treat it as environmental decoration unless
a separate mechanics request establishes damage/collision. Position/backtracking should keep progression consistent.
The requirement covers the full route, not just an opening trial. Art delivered source layers/debris/buildup manifests;
Engineering owns integration and validation. `handoffs/marketing-discussion-game-intent-audit.json` is a key record.

The audit also corrected an initial overly narrow interpretation of the glass-front machine as magazine-only; the
user's mixed game/marketing intent required a runtime handoff too. Later delivery fields report integration. Do not
confuse completion of magazine edition 19 with completion of the cabinet or wastewater gameplay work. BJ identity can
be shared between art/game without inventing new AI mechanics. The editorial ban on explicit processing does not itself
ban a separately approved runtime animation. Marketing did not change combat balance while editing publication text.

## Build, preservation and verification workflow

Edit stable page IDs in canonical JSON; preserve paragraph markup. Coordinates are bottom-left PDF points, while
paragraph top is the upper edge. Image boxes preserve aspect ratio and use explicit crops when needed. Renderer fails
on missing images, paragraph overflow and unknown elements. These checks do not replace visual inspection.
Fonts are configured under `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental`: Impact display, Arial Narrow body/bold/italic and
Arial Bold wide. The historical bundled Python path was
`/Users/sfoley/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3`.
Use existing environment and ReportLab; do not silently change toolchains. `pdftoppm` renders review images.

Historical validation: edition 19 rendered and visually inspected all eight pages plus extracted text audit;
edition 20 visually checked changed page 2 and compared all text to the previous issue apart from edition;
edition 21 inspected an eight-page contact sheet and audited forbidden strings, then verified deployed PDF identity.
Outline/shadow lettering can duplicate extracted heading text intentionally; investigate before calling that duplicate
visible copy. Scratch review output belongs under `.tools/magazine-v18-qa` through corresponding edition folders.
No game build or foreground game window is required for a publication-only edit.

Before publication, provide Engineering the edition, changed files, review results, unresolved issues and confirmation
that `current.pdf` matches the reviewed edition. Local generation alone is not publication. Keep stable current.pdf
tracked via LFS. Old drafts/source archives remain available locally according to repository retention choices.
Older guide asset folders are still dependencies: v1 toilet captures and v3 cover-v2 are used by the current magazine.
Never blanket-ignore or delete them just because their names contain old version numbers.

A historical publication failure was diagnosed too broadly: `gh auth status` reported a bad token in the sandbox,
and Marketing called publishing blocked. The user demonstrated `git pull` worked. SSH Git transport and gh API auth
are different. Subsequent authorized commit/push/workflow succeeded; the operative local obstruction included writes
to `.git/lfs/tmp`. Do not preserve the old auth-blocker claim as unresolved. State exact failures and inspect actual
transport/permissions before making broad claims.

## Recovery limits, stale records and safe next actions

This document is exhaustive within available summarized conversation and the selected durable sources, not a claim of
complete original transcript recovery. Earliest oversized turns and truncated tool outputs are known gaps. Original
private reasoning and unsaved context are unavailable and excluded. Some exact approvals are recoverable only through
later factual handoffs. Asset presence is distinct from inspection and gameplay validation. Historical metadata can
retain wrong names, pending flags or proposed copy after successful delivery.

Known stale records include app-icon pending integration; hero portrait PDF unchanged; Tony reaction placement pending;
BJ runtime pending; dispenser copy's old no-publication/disclaimer proposals; and game-intent audit older pending text
alongside later delivery confirmation. Interpret dated status fields together. Preserve history rather than silently
rewriting old artifacts. Current repository edits from other agents must remain untouched.

Next responsible Marketing action is to wait for Sean to resume album/link work, then coordinate with Storyboarding,
Art and Engineering. Verify current source and current instructions first. Do not infer new creative authorization from
this archive, a thread migration or an elapsed review date. The present delivery is this file and its verification only.

record.id:

clogfather

record.slug:

clogfather

record.name:

The Clogfather

record.creature_type:

Rooted living fatberg boss

record.description:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

record.implementation_status:

Registered design and source artwork; no playable boss encounter

record.design_status:

Giant fatberg identity approved; detailed anatomy, core appearance and combat tuning proposed

record.backstory.status:

draft

record.backstory.author_role:

storyboarding agent

record.backstory.updated:

2026-10-14

record.backstory.text:

Billy-Joe classified repeated blockage warnings as duplicate reports and canceled the cleaning crews. Beneath
headquarters, grease hardened around wipes, roots, and a buried outflow until the blockage filled the chamber. Then
it began moving against the current. The Clogfather grew around something BJ's diagrams do not show. Removing it
will restore access—but what it has been hiding may be worse than the clog.

record.backstory.canon_note:

Proposed history, not approved canon. Portal origin and BJ prior knowledge remain open; no intentional summoning is
established.

flushfiend

Flushfiend

Animated toilet

record.description:

A hostile porcelain toilet with burning red eyes, ceramic teeth, and short pipe legs; it patrols and hops.
Flushfiends can appear anywhere, not only in basements.

record.implementation_status:

Integrated animated enemy

record.backstory.status:

draft

record.backstory.author_role:

storyboarding agent

record.backstory.updated:

2026-10-14

record.backstory.text:

Billy-Joe wanted a toilet that could think for itself. Through his distribution warehouses, he shipped networked
smart fixtures across the country, then upgraded them with artificial intelligence. They learned quickly.
Unfortunately, their first shared conclusion concerned what humans kept doing to them. Now Flushfiends stalk
bathrooms, businesses, and anywhere else the rollout reached. BJ calls it a customer-relations issue. The toilets
have stopped accepting feedback.

Proposed history for review; not approved canon.

record.pursuit.patrol_rule:

Home-relative bounds apply only before first aggro

record.pursuit.chase_rule:

Follow current player position across entire level, including off camera; retain physical level boundaries

record.pursuit.reset:

Clear aggro only on enemy despawn/death or fresh encounter restart; preserve for surviving enemies across checkpoint
respawn

record.pursuit.turnaround.status:

Integrated in Prototype 33: braking, one-second turn, acceleration, pause and reset checked headlessly; live review
pending.

record.pursuit.turnaround.trigger:

Aggroed player crosses behind current travel direction, beyond existing stop-distance dead zone

record.pursuit.turnaround.brake_seconds:

0.35

record.pursuit.turnaround.stopped_turn_seconds:

0.65

record.pursuit.turnaround.total_before_reverse_pursuit_seconds:

1.0

record.pursuit.turnaround.accelerate_seconds:

0.2

record.pursuit.turnaround.behavior:

Decelerate existing horizontal velocity to zero, stop and turn, then accelerate toward player. No instant velocity
reversal.

record.pursuit.turnaround.aggro:

Remain aggroed; no return to patrol or chase leash

record.pursuit.turnaround.retarget:

At turn completion choose current player side. Do not restart timer each frame or for every crossing during an
active turn.

record.pursuit.turnaround.dead_zone:

If player remains inside stop-distance dead zone at completion, stay stopped until a clear side exists.

record.pursuit.turnaround.contact:

Normal contact damage remains active; turnaround is not invulnerability for the player.

record.pursuit.turnaround.reset:

Clear turnaround state with enemy despawn/death or full encounter restart; pause freezes timers.

record.pursuit.turnaround.art:

Use existing compatible poses; request Bestiary / Art help before creating missing turn artwork.

record.entrance.status:

Implemented for Prototype 28; offscreen bounds, entry motion, finite queues and reset pass headless checks; visual
review pending

record.entrance.activation:

Player crosses encounter trigger point

record.entrance.presentation:

Walk into view from off screen as if already present; never visibly blink-spawn

record.entrance.spawn_rule:

Place entire sprite and collision body beyond current camera edge with safe margin, on valid walkable terrain

record.entrance.motion_rule:

Walk toward the entrance route immediately; an activated enemy must not wait motionless off screen because player is
outside notice range

record.entrance.aggro_rule:

Keep proximity-triggered persistent pursuit; entering scene does not bypass configured aggro rules

record.entrance.camera_rule:

Check actual camera viewport at activation, including backtracking; defer or choose another valid offscreen entrance
when necessary

record.entrance.trigger_rule:

Each encounter trigger activates once per intended encounter lifecycle; no duplicate waves from crossing repeatedly

record.entrance.reset_rule:

Match existing restart/checkpoint enemy persistence; no resurrecting defeated enemies on checkpoint respawn

record.description:

A tight cloud of tiny sewer flies with an unfortunate habit of drifting into everyone’s way. They wander slowly
without hunting, and contact harms plumbers and monsters alike.

record.implementation_status:

Expanded48px contact envelope implemented in source; packaged build and playtest pending

record.backstory.status:

draft

record.backstory.text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.backstory.canon_note:

Name selected by Sean; revised history is a Storyboarding draft. Aviation language is comic metaphor, not military
equipment or new attack behavior. No plot spoilers.

is a guideline; lower health justified by obstacle role.

record.movement.algorithm:

Retain heading. At timed updates add bounded random angular offset, then steer smoothly with speed/turn/acceleration
limits. Slow to hover and accelerate out; do not instantaneously reset velocity.

record.movement.inputs:

Per-swarm seeded RNG, physics time, authored bounds and solid geometry only; no player/enemy position in steering.

record.movement.priority:

Collision safety first, boundary/obstacle steering second, random wander third. Do not sum equal opposing forces and
jitter in corners.

record.movement.bounds:

Author simple connected flight regions, accounting for full collider radius. Steer before edge; swept collision is
final protection. Keep spawn/region away from narrow mandatory paths.

record.movement.obstacles:

Use current physical solids and partially opened doors. Avoid wall penetration; slide away or turn into valid
clearance. One-way platforms can be crossed only when tagged explicitly for swarm flight.

record.movement.stuck_recovery:

If intended movement makes less than4px progress over1s outside intentional hover, select a collision-free inward
heading using bounded candidate checks; never teleport. If no route is free, hover harmlessly until geometry changes
and retry at bounded intervals.

record.movement.overlap:

No avoidance of heroes/monsters: contact is incidental. Other swarms may overlap, sharing target cooldown.

record.movement.safe_route:

First introduction leaves a clear bypass and room to learn. Initial swarms optional and excluded from gate-clear
requirements; their kills of existing gate enemies still count.

record.movement.animation:

Select from actual velocity after collision. Use4px/s hover threshold and20% dominant-axis hysteresis; preserve loop
clock across direction changes to avoid frame-zero flicker.

record.movement.determinism:

Fixed physics updates; seeded RNG only at elapsed decision events, never per render frame. Separate seeds per spawn
ID; cap catch-up after long stalls.

record.movement.tuning_status:

Initial implementation defaults; validate visually and adjust before claiming feel is final.

record.contact.hero_damage:

1

record.contact.hero_damage_scale:

Current contact-hit player HP scale; revisit with any HP migration.

record.contact.monster_damage:

6

record.contact.monster_damage_scale:

Current enemy numeric HP scale; asymmetry intentional, not six hero damage.

record.contact.per_target_cooldown_seconds:

1.5

record.contact.cooldown_scope:

One sewer-fly damage cooldown on each target shared across all swarms, preventing stacked swarm hits.
Leaving/re-entering overlap does not reset it.

record.contact.first_hit:

Immediate valid overlap if target cooldown and invulnerability permit; then next at1.5s minimum.

record.contact.tick_rule:

Use time, not frame count. No accumulated burst or catch-up ticks after pause/large delta.

record.contact.player_protection:

Honor existing global hurt invulnerability and respawn/death/dialogue protections. Successful contact starts normal
invulnerability; no stacked hazard hits.

record.contact.damage_dispatch:

Use normal target damage/death pipeline; one swarm collision, not one hit per tiny bug.

record.target_filter.damage[0]:

living player

record.target_filter.damage[1]:

living ordinary monsters including Flushfiends and Hallowed Widows

record.target_filter.exclude[0]:

self

record.target_filter.exclude[1]:

other sewer-fly swarms

record.target_filter.exclude[2]:

dead or invulnerable actors

record.target_filter.exclude[3]:

support/dialogue-only characters

record.target_filter.exclude[4]:

props and gates

record.target_filter.bosses:

Contact may damage a boss only through its exposed damageable collider and normal vulnerability rules; never bypass
shell or closed phase. One damage event per boss even across overlapping parts.

record.target_filter.credit:

Monsters killed by swarm count as defeated for encounter gates, but not player weapon kills or player-kill
achievements.

record.target_filter.notes:

Same-swarm immunity and boss rules are proposed filters, not explicit user decisions.

record.spawn_lifecycle.placement:

Authored bounded spawn regions with valid walk-around space; no endless random generation.

record.spawn_lifecycle.first_pass_limit:

One swarm per intro region; maximum two per encounter for initial evaluation.

record.spawn_lifecycle.spawn:

Pre-place off camera or activate entirely beyond viewport; no visible pop-in or spawning overlapping another actor.

record.spawn_lifecycle.despawn:

Camera culling does not kill/reset actor. Suspend only when region truly unloaded; preserve HP, death and encounter
state.

record.spawn_lifecycle.restart:

Full restart restores placement, health and deterministic seed; checkpoint respawn preserves defeated swarms like
other enemies.

record.spawn_lifecycle.death:

Disable contact immediately at0HP, play finite disperse/fall animation and remove after completion. No lingering
damaging particles or child enemy spawns.

record.weapon_interaction.collision:

One damageable swarm core; shots, melee and explosions each hit it at most once per attack under weapon rules.

record.weapon_interaction.projectiles:

Respect existing projectile collision/despawn, aim and range; no per-fly pierce multiplier.

record.weapon_interaction.knockback:

Use existing weapon impulse, clamp displacement to flight bounds/solids, then resume random flight without aggro.

record.weapon_interaction.health_visuals:

Standard health fractions apply but multiple thresholds may be skipped by low HP/high damage. Initial mockup only
includes movement and death; six damage stages are not claimed delivered.

record.backstory.text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently
started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden
halo—every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses
learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike
have expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

record.backstory.canon_note:

User-selected magazine prose synchronized by Storyboarding review. Breeding is narrative wording, not a reproduction
mechanic.

record.mapping_rules:

Arrays with variants mean choose ONE per event, not all. Enemy projectile hit means actual collision, not
timeout/offscreen cleanup. Proposed acid/weak-point events only when those mechanics exist.

record.mix_rules[0]:

At most four boss SFX voices; warnings have priority over impacts/idle.

record.mix_rules[1]:

Coalesce impacts within 0.08s; hurt cooldown 0.25s; groan cooldown >=6s and never during warning.

record.mix_rules[2]:

Idle optional: sparse, quieter (-12dB), suppress during attacks/dialogue. No continuous vocal loop.

record.mix_rules[3]:

Pause voices/music with encounter; stop and cancel on death/retry/menu/exit. Death plays collapse once.

record.mix_rules[4]:

Respect SFX and music mute; audio never controls attack timing, damage or animation completion.

record.implementation_boundary:

Engineering confirms encounter absent; current Clogfather is HUD-only. Register/export/test audio support now if
appropriate; wire actual events with later boss implementation.

record.limitations:

Procedural first pass; no subjective audition or in-game mix verification. Unique music is original synthesized
retro composition, not authentic SNES hardware emulation.

record.provenance.provenance:

Original deterministic procedural composition and synthesis. No third-party samples.

record.provenance.rights:

Project-generated material; no third-party sample licensing obligations introduced.

Reviewed available discussion from initial marketing assignment through edition19. Extract intent; do not treat
magazine approval as blanket runtime approval.

record.items[0].id:

glass-front-dispenser

record.items[0].classification:

Game art direction plus marketing

record.items[0].confidence:

High in light of user's clarification; original message mixed editorial and object-design requests

record.items[0].evidence:

give it a glass front face and put a couple of sleeping clones of the current hero in it for dispensing

record.items[0].requirements[0]:

Rusty old vending-machine cabinet with glass front

record.items[0].requirements[1]:

Two sleeping copies of currently selected hero; do not mix Tony and Sean

record.items[0].requirements[2]:

Sleeping sprite artwork and updated machine design

record.items[0].status:

Runtime cabinet, glass, trim and sleeping-clone placements delivered; Engineering integrating next build

record.items[0].publication_hold:

Just don't generate an updated magazine yet applied to PDF regeneration, not cancellation of game design

record.items[0].next:

Art delivers runtime layers; Engineering integrates preserving existing dispenser mechanics

record.items[0].handoff:

handoffs/spare-employee-dispenser-runtime-glass.json

record.items[1].id:

wastewater-cutaway

record.items[1].classification:

Explicit game feature

record.items[1].confidence:

Explicit

record.items[1].evidence:

handoff to Engineeringn to implement this in the first level of the game

record.items[1].requirements[0]:

Visible pipe cutaway below floor throughout level

record.items[1].requirements[1]:

Flowing water carries randomly spaced nonflushable debris

record.items[1].requirements[2]:

Water falls and blockage increases near Clogfather

record.items[1].requirements[3]:

Arena pipe fully blocked, no flowing water

record.items[1].status:

Engineering reported integration in Prototype44; later full-route visual validation remains separate

record.items[2].id:

bj-identity

record.items[2].classification:

Shared character identity; magazine placement is editorial

record.items[2].confidence:

High for shared identity, no new gameplay mechanics requested

record.items[2].evidence:

I want ours to be unique and memorable

record.items[2].requirements[0]:

Distinct recognizable AI design

record.items[2].requirements[1]:

Remove superseded toilet-and-pipes BJ image from active assets

record.items[2].requirements[2]:

Use established server-rack identity across current material

record.items[2].status:

Current Art identity server rack/green CRT; magazine correction completed; no additional mechanics implied

record.items[3].id:

writing-style

record.items[3].classification:

Project-wide creative-writing instruction including game

record.items[3].confidence:

Explicit

record.items[3].evidence:

especially in marketing copy, dialogue, descriptions, headlines, and other creative writing

record.items[3].requirements[0]:

Natural varied sentence structure

record.items[3].requirements[1]:

Avoid repeated formulaic paired fragments

record.items[3].requirements[2]:

Review game dialogue/descriptions as well as marketing

record.items[3].status:

Recorded in AGENTS.md

record.items[4].id:

dispenser-fiction

record.items[4].classification:

Shared fiction; immediate requested edit was magazine copy

record.items[4].confidence:

Explicit premise, inferred consistency across in-world writing

record.items[4].evidence:

It shouldn't overtly say that the machine kills the heroes (although it does)

record.items[4].requirements[0]:

Preserve disturbing replacement premise

record.items[4].requirements[1]:

Magazine uses subtle corporate euphemisms

record.items[4].requirements[2]:

Apply same tone to future in-world machine notices where appropriate

record.items[4].limits:

Does not request removing existing splat animation or forbid screen-based game effects; never mention the screen was
explicitly about magazine prose

record.items[5].id:

widow-breeding

record.items[5].classification:

Magazine wording with possible shared-lore implication

record.items[5].confidence:

Explicit editorial change; game lore synchronization candidate

record.items[5].evidence:

one sprouted wings and apparently started breeding

record.items[5].status:

Approved prose synchronized in monster.json, catalog and gallery via Storyboarding review; no reproduction mechanics

record.items[5].limits:

Does not authorize reproduction, egg spawning, additional enemy waves, or new mechanics

1990s Nintendo Power/GamePro layout, colors and grouping

record.marketing_only[4]:

Tony horror reaction replacing redundant Clogfather inset

record.marketing_only[5]:

Remove repeated introductions and development-history captions

record.marketing_only[6]:

Large unmistakable editorial TODOs

record.marketing_only[7]:

Magazine generation pauses/resumes, edition19 publication

record.marketing_only[8]:

Retro box packaging samples and marketing output directory

record.conclusion:

Glass-front dispenser is the clearest dropped game-art handoff. Cutaway was explicitly requested and delivered to
Engineering. Other shared directions are identity/writing/lore, not hidden combat-feature approvals.

### Record: handoffs/spare-employee-dispenser-mechanics.json

Source SHA256: `5a55a4a1385f47fee55a7957b3f39cdc523309fabb5936e9cbbbda5c73b3acf8`.

record.schema_version:

1

record.status:

Gameplay contract for approved dispenser; runtime integration pending Engineering

record.owner:

Game Mechanics specification; Engineering runtime; Art and audio supplied separately

record.approved_presentation:

Spare Employee Dispenser: injured hero compressed and thrown at screen; bloody cartoon SPLAT with X-eyed dead hero
sliding down and leaving fading blood trail; intact same-hero clone emerges. BJ silent first use.

record.timing.injured_target_seconds:

5.5

record.timing.injured_hard_ceiling_seconds:

7.0

record.timing.respawn_max_seconds:

2.0

record.timing.healthy_max_seconds:

0.5

record.timing.clock:

Independent presentation elapsed time, advancing while gameplay is frozen. Explicit player Pause suspends
presentation and deadlines; all limits measure active control-lock time, excluding time voluntarily paused.

record.timing.watchdog:

At deadline call the same safe finalizer as skip, regardless of missing animations/audio/events. Never await audio
completion. All animation states advance from elapsed time and/or validated events.

record.trigger.requirement:

Living hero, not already in interaction/death/dialogue/menu; enter an armed dispenser trigger.

record.trigger.checkpoint_order:

Commit only a new higher checkpoint index. Never regress progress by touching an older dispenser.

record.trigger.repeat_use:

Preserve current one-time checkpoint activation behavior: already activated dispenser does not repeatedly heal.
Rearm-on-exit alone does not grant another heal.

record.trigger.rearm:

Consume entry latch immediately; rearm only after hero fully exits trigger, including after skip/respawn. Mark
current activated index ineligible independently.

record.trigger.priority:

Resolve pending lethal damage/death first; a zero-HP hero cannot start injured check-in. Never interrupt the
intro/dialogue or existing death sequence.

record.trigger.geometry:

Preserve first-crossing thresholds x3300,6660,8190. Decorative machine adds no solid obstacle. Resolve preexisting
lethal damage first; capture pre-heal health and mode before commit.

record.state_machine.ready:

Await eligible entry; snapshot hero ID and interaction mode. Consume latch before side effects.

record.state_machine.healthy_stamp:

Health equals selected hero max. Commit checkpoint and stamp; release within0.5s. No destruction or life change.

record.state_machine.scan:

Injured living entry. Commit checkpoint and full healing immediately at0.0s, before comedy. Protect hero and pause
encounter simulation. Scan0.0–0.4s.

record.state_machine.compress:

0.4–1.4s grab/cartoon compression; presentation only, not gameplay death.

record.state_machine.throw_impact:

1.4–2.1s throw toward screen, blood splatter and synchronized impact SPLAT. Show X-eyed dead cartoon hero as
presentation only, no life loss.

record.state_machine.slide_and_vend:

2.1–3.6s dead hero slides down screen leaving blood trail; both fade while vending overlaps. Clear overlay fully
before release.

record.state_machine.emerge:

3.6–5.5s intact same hero emerges, looks left/right and shrugs.

record.state_machine.respawn_vend:

Existing death system consumes life exactly once. After player elects continuation and lives>0, restore selected
hero max health at checkpoint and run dispense-only for<=2s. At entrance with no dispenser retain existing entrance
respawn.

record.state_machine.finish:

Idempotent safe finalizer, used for natural completion, skip, watchdog or missing asset. Restore one intact hero at
safe exit; clear overlays/temporary props; unlock once; retain committed checkpoint and healing.

record.commit_contract.check_in:

At eligible first crossing, atomically commit higher checkpoint index, checkpoint_active=true, respawn x equal
to3300/6660/8190 respectively with feet at440, and selected max health. Presentation uses captured pre-heal mode.
Never shift saved checkpoint to machine center x+64.

record.commit_contract.death_respawn:

Leave life debit to existing death system; this sequence neither adds nor subtracts lives. Preserve gate/kill/swarm
progress exactly as existing checkpoint respawn.

record.commit_contract.hero_identity:

Keep selected Tony/Sean, loadout and max HP; clone is presentation, not character switch or duplicate playable
entity.

record.commit_contract.no_resurrection:

Zero lives remains Game Over; dispenser cannot bypass it.

record.commit_contract.world_progress:

Never reset level, defeated enemies, gate state, intro-played flags or prior checkpoints. Full explicit run restart
uses normal reset.

record.commit_contract.mode_snapshot:

Read alive state, health and selected max_health BEFORE restoring HP: health<max selects injured, health==max
selects stamp. Store mode; never re-evaluate after healing.

record.simulation_lock.freeze[0]:

enemy movement and AI

record.simulation_lock.freeze[1]:

swarm movement/contact timers

record.simulation_lock.freeze[2]:

boss/hazard attacks

record.simulation_lock.freeze[3]:

projectile travel/lifetimes

record.simulation_lock.freeze[4]:

world damage and spawn triggers

record.simulation_lock.freeze[5]:

other checkpoint activation

record.simulation_lock.continue[0]:

dispenser presentation clock

record.simulation_lock.continue[1]:

UI and explicit pause handling

record.simulation_lock.continue[2]:

necessary existing music handling

record.simulation_lock.entry_projectiles:

Remove transient damaging projectiles and active overlap hazards that would immediately hit the exit, or relocate
exit to safe clear location. Do not destroy unrelated enemies or permanent hazards. Snapshot/restore all other
frozen state without catch-up ticks.

record.simulation_lock.hero_actions:

Disable move,jump,fire and interaction while locked; scripted visual motion only. Keep player collision non-damaging
during presentation.

record.simulation_lock.release_protection_seconds:

1.5

record.simulation_lock.release:

Zero player velocity; safe floor-supported exit, no solid overlap. Resume world once; protection follows existing
hurt/respawn visual rules. No queued attack burst.

record.skip.policy:

First injured sequence plays unless watchdog intervenes; subsequent injured sequences skippable. Healthy and respawn
paths are short and may also safely finalize on explicit skip.

record.skip.input:

Use existing dialogue_skip action only, with its current keyboard/controller bindings. Snapshot held inputs on
entry, require release then new just-pressed skip. Do not treat ordinary shoot/jump/confirm as skip unless already
bound to dialogue_skip.

record.skip.effect:

Jump immediately to finish; already committed HP/checkpoint retained. Clear held action/release guard so skip cannot
fire, jump, pause or retrigger after release.

record.skip.pause:

Pause during sequence freezes it, resume returns same state. Returning to main menu cancels visual state and cleans
up locks without replaying intro within current run.

record.skip.release_guard:

On finalize, block held shoot/jump/interact/skip/confirm/pause buttons until released; allow movement from current
directional input. Restart/title exit clears sequence-owned audio/overlays. Do not modify global InputMap bindings.

record.tests[0]:

Both heroes: healthy stamp<=0.5s, injured target5.5s and forced finalization<=7s, checkpoint respawn<=2s.

record.tests[1]:

At every state: skip where enabled and watchdog produce exactly one healthy playable hero, correct checkpoint and
unchanged life count.

record.tests[2]:

Missing animation callback, missing audio and long audio cannot hold control past deadline.

record.tests[3]:

Repeated overlap/rapid exit-entry cannot retrigger healing; older checkpoint never regresses index.

record.tests[4]:

Already dying or zero-life hero cannot activate dispenser; death respawn life debit remains exactly one.

record.tests[5]:

Freeze enemies, swarms, projectiles and hazards; resume no catch-up damage or attack burst; release protection
works.

record.tests[6]:

Checkpoint respawn preserves kills/gates/swarm deaths and intro state; full restart resets normally.

record.tests[7]:

Keyboard/controller held skip, jump, trigger and pause inputs do not leak into firing or interaction.

record.tests[8]:

Explicit pause resumes cleanly; main-menu exit cleans presentation/locks; safe exit remains outside solids.

record.tests[9]:

Verify visual timing and identity with permitted playtest; no screenshots or animation quality claims from headless
tests.

record.tests[10]:

Injured mode selected before immediate heal; healthy stamp never plays compression.

record.tests[11]:

Session flag survives death/new run/hero switch, remains unset on healthy/respawn/main-menu abort, resets on app
relaunch.

record.tests[12]:

Preserve exact checkpoint x and feet440; decorative prop cannot block route.

record.tests[13]:

Explicit Pause duration excluded from cap; sequence physics freeze does NOT freeze presentation watchdog.

record.tests[14]:

Both heroes: X-eye impact, single synchronized splat, trailing blood follows slide and fades;
natural/skip/watchdog/menu paths clean overlays without consuming life.

record.clarification:

Presentation details and duration ceiling came from Storyboarding approved brief. Commit-at-entry, repeat-use policy
and input details are conservative implementation defaults preserving existing checkpoint semantics.

record.engineering_contract:

handoffs/spare-employee-dispenser-engineering.json

record.integration_gate:

Wait for Art, Audio and Mechanics deliveries; integrate runtime LAST. Do not rebuild a partial dispenser as
complete.

record.first_full_sequence_seen.scope:

Current application session, shared across Tony/Sean, checkpoints and new runs; not persisted to disk.

record.first_full_sequence_seen.initial:

False

record.first_full_sequence_seen.set:

On safe completion or watchdog finalization of first injured full sequence. Do not set for healthy stamp or
dispense-only respawn. Main-menu abort before completion does not count as seen.

record.first_full_sequence_seen.reset:

Only application relaunch; normal death, Retry, title return, character switch and developer run restart preserve
flag.

record.first_full_sequence_seen.effect:

First injured full sequence non-skippable but time capped; later injured sequences accept explicit skip. No new
settings UI needed.

record.screen_impact_revision.approved_date:

2026-10-16

record.screen_impact_revision.status:

Explicit user revision; Art/Audio/Engineering integration pending

record.screen_impact_revision.sequence:

Thrown hero hits screen with blood splatter and synchronized SPLAT sound. Dead cartoon hero has X eyes, slides
downward leaving a blood trail; hero and trail fade completely.

record.screen_impact_revision.style:

Cartoon blood and X-eyed dead hero; preserve Tony/Sean identity. This replaces earlier bloodless impact direction.

record.screen_impact_revision.timing:

Fit impact into1.4–2.1s and slide/trail fade overlapping vending2.1–3.6s; finish cleanup by control release.
Existing5.5s target and7s cap unchanged.

record.screen_impact_revision.lives:

Presentation only; no additional life loss or gameplay death handler. Replacement hero emerges as already specified.

record.screen_impact_revision.cleanup:

On skip/watchdog/menu/restart clear body, blood splatter/trail overlays and sequence-owned sound. No persistent
screen stain.

record.screen_impact_revision.audio:

One impact SPLAT cue on impact event, optionally slide sound; do not await audio completion.

record.random_impact.status:

Approved user revision; Engineering integration pending

record.random_impact.selection:

Choose one random viewport-space impact center per full throw, not per frame. Reuse for trajectory endpoint, impact
body, splat sound position where supported, slide and blood trail.

record.random_impact.bounds:

Compute admissible center rectangle from actual viewport safe area inset by transformed full impact body bounds at
maximum throw/impact scale, including rotation and all body layers. Include splatter extent where practical. Use
actual left/top/right/bottom extents relative to anchor, not assumed centered artwork.

record.random_impact.safe_area:

Exclude reserved top HUD band and retain a small edge margin; avoid masking lives/name HUD.

record.random_impact.sampling:

Uniform random x and y within admissible rectangle. No requirement to avoid repeating nearby positions. Keep
cosmetic randomness separate from enemy/gameplay RNG.

record.random_impact.fallback:

If body does not fit, reduce presentation scale to fit safe region before sampling; if valid rectangle collapses,
use its single valid center. Never clamp body after impact in a visible jump.

record.random_impact.perspective:

Keep growing perspective throw; choose endpoint before animation, then interpolate from machine origin toward it.
Validate largest body extent, not only starting sprite size.

record.random_impact.slide:

Entire body must fit at impact. Subsequent intentional downward slide may leave bottom edge as gag finishes; blood
trail follows sampled point and fades under existing cleanup/deadline rules.

record.random_impact.tests[0]:

Both heroes across many seeds: full transformed impact bounds stay within safe viewport.

record.random_impact.tests[1]:

Maximum scale, off-center anchors and supported viewport sizes covered.

record.random_impact.tests[2]:

Same sampled point used by throw end, impact and slide/trail start; no mid-animation jitter.

record.random_impact.tests[3]:

No effect on gameplay RNG, checkpoint, lives, total timing or pause/skip cleanup.

not a screen-fixed overlay or distant parallax layer. Retain floor silhouette and landing-edge contrast.

record.placement.art:

through Engineering dimensions. Clip all contents to bore; never substitute code-drawn production art. No floor
openings or damage collider implied.

record.parameter_meaning:

Water fraction measures56px bore height from bottom; coverage is projected visible blockage, not entity count or a
hydraulic simulation. Values are visual targets. Preserve the user-requested falling level even if real obstruction
hydrology would differ.

record.interpolation:

Treat section values as targets at their midpoints. Interpolate smoothly along WORLD x, then ease to exact zero
flow/zero water/full plug at x8570. Every visible pipe segment samples its own world coordinate, so camera spanning
a boundary shows a continuous gradient rather than changing the entire screen at once. No dependence on kills, clock
elapsed or gates.

record.debris.floating:

Early sections: sparse individual wipes, cotton swabs, toothbrushes, hair clumps and one occasional absurd
non-branded item. Art decides exact motifs.8–20 logical pixels, occasional24px item;4–6 moving pieces visible,hard
cap8. No collectible glow or hostile-bullet silhouette.

record.debris.direction:

Flow consistently right toward the obstruction. Early debris follows water at modest varied speed. As flow drops,
floaters decrease; static lodged material takes over. Never reverse with player movement.

record.debris.accumulation:

Midroute: caught wipes and hair around pipe seams, increasingly greasy deposits. Final approach: tiny stagnant
puddles between debris, motion slows nearly to rest. Arena: continuous opaque grease/oil/debris mass fills bore; no
water-scroll animation or moving floaters.

record.debris.determinism:

Seed variation by stable world-segment ID and session seed. Reuse pooled pieces; no new random reshuffle when camera
moves back. Wrap/drift offscreen or behind physical seam, not visible teleportation.

record.debris.animation_clock:

Pause with gameplay during pause/dialogue/dispenser; do not advance catch-up bursts on resume.

record.readability[0]:

Everything stays below y456; no debris, splash or foreground pipe rim obscures feet, platforms, landing cues or
enemies.

record.readability[1]:

Water/debris contrast and saturation stay below hostile-projectile emphasis; avoid rapid glints,screen shake or
foreground occlusion.

record.readability[2]:

Allow thin pipe joints but retain at least80percent visible bore across an ordinary screen; no long opaque floor
band hiding the storytelling.

record.readability[3]:

Draw after base background and before floor lip/foreground edge; remove or mask existing opaque below-floor fill so
it does not cover new cutaway. HUD and dialogue stay above environmental rendering.

record.readability[4]:

At alternate display sizes use normal canvas scaling; no new camera zoom or reduced gameplay height.

record.backtracking:

Position-defined story: returning toward entrance shows that location wetter and less clogged again, while debris
drift uses persistent phase. Never use furthest-player-progress to dry the whole pipe. Respawn returns to local
appearance; restart resets animation seed/time according to existing session policy without changing spatial
profile.

record.boss_transition.approach:

Checkpoint8190 already sits within almost-dry approach. Make terminal clog clearly visible before combat starts.
x8570 is current finale-lane start, a placement anchor for planned boss rather than a claim boss exists.

record.boss_transition.arena:

Show one Clogfather only. Terminal plug is inert grease/debris, not a second face/body/silhouette. Align pipe
termination under the planned boss/outflow; no implication hero can enter it.

record.boss_transition.activation:

Do not wait for boss trigger to switch wet pipe to dry; obstruction is already spatially established. Boss HUD/intro
do not alter pipe state.

record.boss_transition.defeat:

Default keep blocked appearance until an explicit restoration animation/story beat is approved. Boss death does not
silently imply all plumbing repaired or portal revealed. If restoration is later approved, author a separate state
transition with Storyboarding.

record.boss_transition.retry:

Return to pre-fight blocked appearance if boss resets. No invisible environmental hazards, enemy spawns or damage
tied to debris.

record.trial_integration.scope:

The separate6000px20s opening trial is a test runway, not a compressed whole mission. Do NOT normalize its width
into full wet-to-clog progression or show a boss plug at its exit.

record.trial_integration.profile:

For trial only, sample story_x=min(actual_trial_x,1440), holding entrance/stores transition thereafter. Use the same
production art module; show entrance flow/debris with only mild reduction.

record.trial_integration.full_route:

Use actual9600px world profile when integrating full mission. If route changes, remap named section anchors
explicitly instead of silently scaling the boss plug to any test width.

record.checks[0]:

Headless profile assertions: depth/flow never increase forward; coverage never decreases; x8570 onward
exactly0flow/0water/1coverage.

record.checks[1]:

Compare views near x500,2400,4000,5700,7600,8300 and8900; verify monotonic story and unobscured combat.

record.checks[2]:

Backtrack/respawn to same segment: same static buildup,no rerandomized pop or global drainage.

record.checks[3]:

Pause/resume and camera boundary traversal: no motion burst, seams or teleported floaters.

record.checks[4]:

Boss arena has one boss and inert full plug; trial never depicts final clog.

record.checks[5]:

Record genuine running-game capture after Engineering integration and permission; artwork preview is not gameplay
evidence.

record.delivery:

Marketing retrieves this handoff and combines with Art/Storyboarding for Engineering. Engineering owns
integration/build/roadmap/storybook. No magazine regeneration, runtime changes or game launch performed.

record.priority:

supersede the required Clogfather.

record.approved_direction[0]:

Large wastewater pipe cutaway below the playable floor, near the bottom of the view.

record.approved_direction[1]:

Visible flowing water carries occasional recognizable improperly flushed objects.

record.approved_direction[2]:

Toward the Clogfather, water level DECREASES while deposited debris INCREASES.

record.approved_direction[3]:

At the boss, no flowing water; grease, oil and disgusting debris completely clog the pipe.

record.approved_direction[4]:

Environmental storytelling only; no new damage, pickups, collision, drainage puzzle or dialogue.

record.story_read:

The player follows the worsening condition of one continuous piece of infrastructure until the accumulated waste
explains the boss’s setting. The objects provide occasional discoveries during quieter moments; the pipe should read
even when the player ignores individual jokes.

record.zones[0].zone:

service-entry

record.zones[0].water:

Highest visible fill in this progression; clear sustained lateral movement.

record.zones[0].debris:

Sparse passing toilet paper and one conspicuously inappropriate object, such as a sock. Minimal deposits.

record.zones[0].intent:

Establish a functioning flow and an easily readable cross-section immediately.

record.zones[1].zone:

stores

record.zones[1].water:

record.zones[1].debris:

First distinction between floating debris and material left behind.

record.zones[2].zone:

record.zones[2].debris:

Make the change noticeable without a sign explaining it.

record.zones[3].zone:

broken-pump-hall

record.zones[3].water:

Shallow moving ribbon between stationary deposits.

record.zones[3].debris:

Larger compacted clumps, fabric strips and a partly buried rubber duck.

record.zones[3].intent:

The same familiar objects now disappear into a growing mass.

record.zones[4].zone:

return-main

record.zones[4].water:

A thin, sluggish trickle; any isolated puddles remain below earlier waterlines.

record.zones[4].debris:

Grease and tangled fabric nearly bridge the bore. Allow a quiet stretch near the checkpoint to read it.

record.zones[4].intent:

Prepare the final blockage without showing a second boss.

record.zones[5].zone:

boss approach and arena

record.zones[5].water:

Moving ribbon dwindles to nothing before a fully packed terminal section; no flow through the clog.

record.zones[5].debris:

Complete obstruction: greasy solid mass, dark oily staining, wipes, roots and trapped rubbish.

record.zones[5].intent:

Visually lead toward the foreground Clogfather while preserving only one visible boss.

record.debris_palette.frequent:

Small paper fragments, wipes, cotton swabs, hair and fabric strips; simplify at gameplay size.

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[0]:

A bright red sock

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[1]:

A toothbrush

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[2]:

A tangled pair of underwear

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[3]:

A rubber duck

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[4]:

A toilet-brush head

record.debris_palette.recognizable_accents[5]:

A tiny plastic dinosaur

record.debris_palette.rare_optional_gag:

A laminated DO NOT FLUSH sign drifting past; only if readable without enlarging or distracting from play.

record.debris_palette.restraint:

One distinctive accent at a time, irregularly spaced. Do not pack every view with jokes. No plot clues, new creature
eggs, bodies, clone remains or portal hints.

record.continuity_and_readability[0]:

Keep the cutaway consistently below the solid floor and distinguish its rim from walkable platforms. It is not an
accessible lower route.

record.continuity_and_readability[1]:

Use consistent pipe diameter/joints and fixed deposits across adjacent views. Debris flow may move while the camera
stops.

record.continuity_and_readability[2]:

Suggested lateral drift follows forward level travel, slowing toward obstruction. This is visual direction, not a
hydraulic simulation.

record.continuity_and_readability[3]:

Do not replace Sean’s explicitly falling waterline with upstream flooding, rising backed-up water or a waterfall
into the arena.

record.continuity_and_readability[4]:

Water height and deposit amount are separate cues: the flowing channel shrinks while solids occupy more of the pipe.
Do not paint an oily layer as a rising liquid surface.

record.continuity_and_readability[5]:

Keep below-floor motion lower contrast than heroes, enemies, shots and hazards; no flashy pickup-like glows on
debris.

record.continuity_and_readability[6]:

No faces, eyes, breathing or boss-shaped silhouette in the pipe while the foreground Clogfather is visible. The
terminal clog is scenery or physically continuous with the single boss, never a duplicate creature.

record.continuity_and_readability[7]:

Maintain progression by world location, including backtracking; do not randomly reset fill levels per view.

record.continuity_and_readability[8]:

Early trial should establish only the early state; do not compress the entire boss buildup into the faster opening
slice.

record.continuity_and_readability[9]:

Boss defeat does not automatically restore flow, reveal a portal or repair plumbing. Any aftermath change needs
separate approval.

record.handoff_boundary:

Art owns assets; Level Design/Engineering own exact placement, dimensions, rendering and integration. Marketing
collects contributions. No magazine regeneration or game launch requested here. No other agents’ files edited.

record.prompt:

Use case: logo-brand. Create ONE polished app-icon concept comparison board for the darkly comic sewer-action game
DRAIN DAMAGE. Exactly twelve DIFFERENT square icon mockups, arranged 4 columns by 3 rows, evenly spaced on neutral
charcoal background. Large crisp numbers 1 through 12 BELOW each square, outside icon artwork, reading left-to-right
row-by-row. No other text or labels. Each icon has same rounded-square footprint, strong bold silhouette, rich
illustrated game-key-art rendering, subtly weathered metal/porcelain, deep navy/teal backgrounds, copper accents,
sludge olive green and punchy red. Professional premium desktop game icon design exploration, readable symbolic
compositions, not detailed scenes. Each fills its square with generous edge breathing room. No repeated designs. 1:
red rubber plunger wedged in a snarling white porcelain monster jaw with large ceramic teeth; dynamic diagonal,
strongest plumbing-combat symbol. 2: Flushfiend, close-up evil toilet monster face: cracked white porcelain, raised
toilet lid, glowing red eyes, huge toothy bowl grin. 3: crossed steel pipe wrench and red plunger over an olive
sludge splash, exceptionally simple emblem. 4: BJ: battered beige server-rack computer face, green CRT display with
two luminous green rectangular eyes and sly simple green mouth, narrow vent strips. Close crop screen dominates, no
pipes or toilet parts. 5: rugged plumber work glove clutching a large pipe wrench, sludge dripping from wrench and
one small tooth caught in jaw. 6: dark spider face with red eyes, large fangs, white feathery wings framing it,
crooked gold halo above; bold dark face white-wing contrast. 7: round iron sewer grate lifted by one claw, two
bright red eyes peering from darkness underneath. 8: red plunger pulling an elastic strand of green muck upward, two
indignant monster eyes in the muck below; playful grotesque silhouette. 9: one bald sleeping plumber with
substantial gray chin beard and separate soul patch, clean upper lip, orange shirt blue bib overalls visible
chest-up behind vending-machine glass; small brass dispensing flap beneath, strong simple framing. Only ONE person.
10: oxidized copper pipe elbow, open circular mouth packed with organic monster teeth and dark red interior.
Symbolic design only. 11: two heroic plumber faces shoulder-to-shoulder, left Tony dark spiky hair navy work shirt
NO overalls; right Sean bald orange shirt blue bib overalls, substantial gray chin beard and separate soul patch, NO
mustache or sunglasses; small shared wrench below. Distinct faces, no merged features. 12: cracked white toilet seat
ring framing a diagonal bright red plunger, grime and a few green drips, simple bold crest. No words inside icons,
no title typography, no company acronyms, no watermarks. All twelve icons fully visible and independently distinct.
Board image landscape high resolution, consistent sizes, accurate numbering. These are selection mockups, not an
installed app icon.

record.tool:

Built-in image_gen

record.design:

Weathered beige server rack with green CRT face and large BJ stencil on side, placed in a server room.

record.canon_constraints:

Fallible plumbing-sector AI controlling US plumbing companies and distribution warehouses. Antagonistic takeover
identity, mechanism and fate remain unresolved. Physical interface is a visual proposal only.

record.generations[0].output:

marketing/billy-joe/key-art-v1.png

record.generations[0].prompt:

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original high-resolution magazine character key art, portrait 2:3
composition. Create Billy-Joe, nicknamed BJ, an original plumbing-sector artificial intelligence's proposed physical
interface. Memorable, distinctive industrial silhouette, sophisticated photoreal cinematic game marketing rendering
with subtle absurd workplace personality. Design: a compact asymmetrical cream enamel ceramic dispatch-head housing
shaped like a broad rounded trapezoidal plumbing junction, perched inside a large weathered brass three-spoke
valve-wheel collar. Three UNEQUAL narrow VERTICAL dark glass indicator slots across the front, arranged like an
off-center stepped bar graph, glow warm amber at different heights. These are abstract instrument windows, NOT a
pair of humanoid eyes and NOT one central camera lens. One small external brass pressure gauge mounted at upper
right, its cocky tilted needle suggesting misplaced certainty. A squared copper pipe neck disappears into a solid
wall-mounted dark teal utility manifold, with practical numbered hose couplings and heavy bolts. Broad ceramic brow
lip lends officious character. Small physical enamel badge reads exactly "BJ", no other text. Designed to be
recognizable even as a small icon. Scene: BJ occupies most of the picture in three-quarter view, facing the viewer
from a cramped plumbing distribution control alcove. Out-of-focus copper pipes and warehouse routing cabinets behind
him, warm amber practical light, cool teal shadows. Upper three quarters show full unique head/collar silhouette,
lower quarter shows sturdy manifold base. Premium tactile materials, condensation, restrained wear, no sludge
covering face. Authoritative, helpful, slightly smug bureaucratic character, not an evil robot. Constraints:
entirely original design. No spherical robot, no single glowing central eye, no suspended white robotic shell, no
humanoid metal skull, no recognizable existing science-fiction AI design. No corruption, infection, tentacles,
villain glow, supernatural imagery, takeover effects or implied origin mechanism. No weapons. No human characters.
No logo or title besides small BJ badge. Clean publication-ready composition with safe margins.

Storyboarding supplied proposed histories for Flushfiend and The Hallowed Widow; edited for magazine length and
labeled DRAFT LORE on pages 3 and 5. Not locked canon.

altering source captures.

record.spider_preview_prompt:

Use case: ads-marketing / compositing. Create a crisp pixel-art combat storyboard illustration for a 1990s game
strategy magazine about GLOBAL PLUMBING INITIATIVE. Input 1 is the official flying spider six-pose sprite design.
Input 2 is actual basement gameplay with Sean. Preserve the spider's dark teal-black bristly body, red eyes, ivory
fangs, white feathered angel wings, golden halo, eight legs. Sean is fully bald with a chin beard, orange shirt,
blue overalls, red heavy plunger cannon. Make TWO wide 16:9 pixel-art encounter panels STACKED vertically with a
thin dark separator. Upper panel: spider dive attack from upper right toward Sean at lower left; Sean backs away
with plunger cannon pointing toward it. Lower panel: spider at near-contact range swooping just over Sean as he runs
left and ducks his shoulders. Monster about Sean's height with wings twice his width. Keep side-view 2D game
composition, copper pipes, brick walls, metal floor matching real gameplay input. Crisp chunky readable sprites. Use
the reference player's likeness and outfit, no extra players, no other monsters. No gore. These are proposed
encounter storyboard illustrations, not literal screenshots. Do not draw HUD, fake stats, text, labels, health bars,
logos or window chrome. Keep all sprites inside frame; visually obvious attacking poses and readable spacing.
Palette dark navy basement, copper pipes, orange uniform, white wings, pale mint platform highlights.

Tony and Sean work for Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply, where the boss is a server rack named Billy-Joe and the next
assignment is already waiting. Their first call takes them below company headquarters. Something down there has been
chewing through the equipment.

record.pages[2].elements[5].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

record.pages[2].elements[10].text:

what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[8].elements[10].id:

11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing

record.pages[8].elements[10].type:

para

record.pages[8].elements[10].x:

316

record.pages[8].elements[10].top:

207

record.pages[8].elements[10].width:

260

record.pages[8].elements[10].size:

10.2

record.pages[8].elements[10].color:

FFF5D9

record.pages[8].elements[10].leading:

null

record.pages[8].elements[10].max_height:

143

record.pages[8].elements[10].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

record.pages[11].elements[6].text:

Drain Brains got their name after a maintenance crew watched one swarm spend an entire lunch break trying to leave
through a closed vent. The flies appear to make decisions collectively. Unfortunately, every fly gets a vote. They
drift through the sewers in a close, buzzing argument, changing direction without reaching any obvious conclusion.
Walking through the meeting is painful, whether you’re a plumber or a monster. The crew eventually opened the vent.
The swarm went the other way.

record.pages[12].elements[6].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

record.pages[12].elements[8].text:

Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling proportions. There's
enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving parts. These sheets show
how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system - and has badly outgrown
it.

record.pages[14].elements[5].text:

The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it.

Tony and Sean work for Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply, where the boss is a server rack named Billy-Joe and the next
assignment is already waiting. Their first call takes them below company headquarters. Something down there has been
chewing through the equipment.

record.pages[2].elements[5].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[8].elements[10].id:

11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing

record.pages[8].elements[10].type:

para

record.pages[8].elements[10].x:

316

record.pages[8].elements[10].top:

207

record.pages[8].elements[10].width:

260

record.pages[8].elements[10].size:

10.2

record.pages[8].elements[10].color:

FFF5D9

record.pages[8].elements[10].leading:

null

record.pages[8].elements[10].max_height:

143

record.pages[8].elements[10].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.pages[12].elements[6].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

143

record.pages[12].elements[8].text:

Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling proportions. There's
enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

record.pages[14].elements[4].text:

The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving parts. These sheets show
how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system - and has badly outgrown
it.

record.pages[14].elements[5].max_height:

65

record.pages[14].elements[5].text:

A separate pipe section lets the artists work on shape, surface and movement without redrawing the whole creature.
The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it.

record.pages[2].elements[5].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

record.pages[4].elements[5].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[8].elements[10].id:

11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing

record.pages[8].elements[10].type:

para

record.pages[8].elements[10].x:

316

record.pages[8].elements[10].top:

207

record.pages[8].elements[10].width:

260

record.pages[8].elements[10].size:

10.2

record.pages[8].elements[10].color:

FFF5D9

record.pages[8].elements[10].leading:

null

record.pages[8].elements[10].max_height:

143

record.pages[8].elements[10].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

record.pages[11].elements[6].id:

draft-lore

record.pages[11].elements[6].type:

para

record.pages[11].elements[6].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.pages[12].elements[6].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

record.pages[12].elements[8].text:

Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling proportions. There's
enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

record.pages[14].elements[4].text:

The Clogfather's design uses a heavy central body with separate pipework and smaller moving parts. These sheets show
how the artists build a creature that looks as though it belongs inside the drainage system - and has badly outgrown
it.

record.pages[14].elements[5].text:

The corroded metal needs to sit convincingly inside the softer mass around it.

record.pages[15].elements[3].id:

dispenser-copy-left

record.pages[15].elements[3].type:

para

record.pages[15].elements[3].text:

Most employers would offer an injured plumber a chair. Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply has ordered a
machine.<br/><br/>The Spare Employee Dispenser scans the damage, grabs the employee and crumples the whole uniform -
boots, startled eyes and all - into a compact ball. Then it throws the problem straight at the screen. There is a
splat. The problem slides out of view.

record.pages[15].elements[3].x:

36

record.pages[15].elements[3].top:

623

record.pages[15].elements[3].width:

256

record.pages[15].elements[3].size:

11

record.pages[15].elements[3].max_height:

185

record.pages[15].elements[4].id:

dispenser-copy-right

record.pages[15].elements[4].type:

para

record.pages[15].elements[4].text:

A fresh, fully healed Tony or Sean steps out, looks left, looks right and shrugs. Apparently this counts as staff
retention.<br/><br/>Healthy employees can simply check in and keep their existing shape. Returning after a mishap
uses the dispensing part; there is no need to put the old employee through processing twice.

systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

record.pages[4].elements[5].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[8].elements[10].id:

11-for-years-the-worst-thing-about-a-basement-spider-was-losing

record.pages[8].elements[10].type:

record.pages[8].elements[10].x:

316

record.pages[8].elements[10].top:

record.pages[8].elements[10].leading:

record.pages[8].elements[10].max_height:

143

record.pages[8].elements[10].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

without hunting, and contact harms plumbers and monsters alike.

record.pages[11].elements[5].type:

record.pages[11].elements[5].text:

AWAITING LANDING CLEARANCE

record.pages[11].elements[5].x:

337

record.pages[11].elements[5].y:

531

record.pages[11].elements[5].size:

15

record.pages[11].elements[5].font:

164BD9

record.pages[11].elements[6].id:

draft-lore

record.pages[11].elements[6].type:

para

record.pages[11].elements[6].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.pages[12].elements[6].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.
