record.pages[12].elements[8].text:

Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling proportions. There's
enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

YOUR REPLACEMENT

record.pages[15].elements[2].font:

record.pages[15].elements[3].id:

dispenser-copy-left

record.pages[15].elements[3].type:

para

record.pages[15].elements[3].text:

Most employers would offer an injured plumber a chair. Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply has ordered a
machine.<br/><br/>The Spare Employee Dispenser scans the damage, grabs the employee and crumples the whole uniform -
boots, startled eyes and all - into a compact ball. Then it throws the problem straight at the screen. There is a
splat. The problem slides out of view.

record.pages[15].elements[3].x:

36

record.pages[15].elements[3].top:

623

record.pages[15].elements[3].width:

256

record.pages[15].elements[3].size:

11

record.pages[15].elements[3].max_height:

185

record.pages[15].elements[4].id:

dispenser-copy-right

record.pages[15].elements[4].type:

para

record.pages[15].elements[4].text:

A fresh, fully healed Tony or Sean steps out, looks left, looks right and shrugs. Apparently this counts as staff
retention.<br/><br/>Healthy employees can simply check in and keep their existing shape. Returning after a mishap
uses the dispensing part; there is no need to put the old employee through processing twice.

GamePro.

record.pages[1].elements[25].type:

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

record.pages[1].elements[27].text:

what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

record.pages[2].elements[13].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[13].x:

198

record.pages[2].elements[13].top:

632

record.pages[2].elements[13].width:

184

record.pages[2].elements[13].size:

11.4

record.pages[2].elements[13].color:

111421

record.pages[2].elements[13].max_height:

159

record.pages[2].elements[13].leading:

12.768000000000002

record.pages[2].elements[14].id:

management-maintenance-015

record.pages[2].elements[14].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Most employers would offer an injured plumber a chair. Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply has ordered a
machine.<br/><br/>The Spare Employee Dispenser scans the damage, grabs the employee and crumples the whole uniform -
boots, startled eyes and all - into a compact ball. Then it throws the problem straight at the screen. There is a
splat. The problem slides out of view.

record.pages[2].elements[27].text:

A fresh, fully healed Tony or Sean steps out, looks left, looks right and shrugs. Apparently this counts as staff
retention.<br/><br/>Healthy employees can simply check in and keep their existing shape. Returning after a mishap
uses the dispensing part; there is no need to put the old employee through processing twice.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

para

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[12].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

record.pages[4].elements[13].text:

enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

record.pages[4].elements[20].type:

para

record.pages[4].elements[20].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

record.editorial_guidance.audience:

People who love games; no technical background assumed.

record.editorial_guidance.rule:

No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.

record.editorial_guidance.keep_internal:

Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README
only.

record.editorial_guidance.qualifications:

Use compact plain English: Preview artwork - not a screenshot; Shown in an earlier version of the game; An idea we
are exploring. Coming in a future update only when committed.

record.editorial_guidance.preserve:

Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.

record.editorial_guidance.writing_style:

Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations.
Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

record.pages[1].elements[25].type:

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

24

record.pages[1].elements[27].text:

Plumbing runs in Tony's family. He brings that accumulated knowledge to the job, along with the patience to explain
what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

record.pages[2].elements[13].type:

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.

record.pages[2].elements[26].id:

management-maintenance-027

record.pages[2].elements[26].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Most employers would offer an injured plumber a chair. Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply has ordered a
machine.<br/><br/>The Spare Employee Dispenser scans the damage, grabs the employee and crumples the whole uniform -
boots, startled eyes and all - into a compact ball. Then it throws the problem straight at the screen. The ball hits
with a splat and slides out of view.

record.pages[2].elements[26].x:

24

record.pages[2].elements[26].top:

273

record.pages[2].elements[26].width:

196

record.pages[2].elements[27].id:

management-maintenance-028

record.pages[2].elements[27].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[27].text:

A fresh, fully healed Tony or Sean steps out, looks left, looks right and shrugs. Apparently this counts as staff
retention.<br/><br/>Healthy employees can simply check in and keep their existing shape. Returning after a mishap
uses the dispensing part; there is no need to put the old employee through processing twice.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

para

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one spread its wings. The Hallowed
Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail
attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too.
Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what
this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[12].text:

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into
the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences
back at anyone approaching.

record.pages[4].elements[13].type:

para

record.pages[4].elements[13].text:

Grease, wipes, roots, and discarded rubbish have packed together into a fatberg of appalling proportions. There's
enough ordinary drain trouble in that heap to keep a crew busy for days. Unfortunately, the heap is moving. Give it
room.

record.pages[4].elements[20].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

record.editorial_guidance.audience:

People who love games; no technical background assumed.

record.editorial_guidance.rule:

No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.

record.editorial_guidance.keep_internal:

Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README
only.

record.editorial_guidance.qualifications:

Picture captions should describe the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss
development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and
development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea
captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.

record.editorial_guidance.preserve:

Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.

record.editorial_guidance.writing_style:

Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations.
Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

record.editorial_guidance.corporate_horror:

Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not
disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other
fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.

record.editorial_guidance.pending_revision:

October 16: dispenser copy revised after edition 18. Hold PDF regeneration until the user requests it; collect
further feedback in this source. Published edition 18 remains unchanged.

record.editorial_guidance.todos:

Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous
high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small
italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay
is unfinished.

record.editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision:

Keep the first description unchanged. Removed repetitive second introduction and redundant idle inset. Art
requested: Tony gaping/recoiling toward the large portrait on his right. Replace the conspicuous TODO with delivered
artwork and inspect its scale/gaze at the next authorized regeneration.

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

record.pages[2].elements[13].type:

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[13].x:

198

record.pages[2].elements[13].top:

632

record.pages[2].elements[13].width:

184

record.pages[2].elements[14].type:

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply is pleased to announce a new approach to employee welfare. The Spare Employee
Dispenser promises to have Tony and Sean fit for duty with a minimum of paperwork.<br/><br/>The brochure calls the
procedure "staff renewal." It devotes considerably more space to the reduction in sick leave than to what happens
during an appointment.

24

record.pages[2].elements[27].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[27].text:

they were looking for appears to be outside the scope of the brochure.<br/><br/>BJ considers the matter settled. The
next service call is already on the schedule.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently
started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo
- every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned
to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have
expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[18].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and
development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea
captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.

record.editorial_guidance.preserve:

Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.

record.editorial_guidance.writing_style:

Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations.
Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

record.editorial_guidance.corporate_horror:

Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not
disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other
fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.

record.editorial_guidance.pending_revision:

Feedback through October 16 incorporated into edition 19; regeneration authorized.

record.editorial_guidance.todos:

Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous
high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small
italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay
is unfinished.

record.editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision:

First description preserved; redundant paragraph and idle inset replaced with Tony horror reaction.

record.pages[1].elements[25].type:

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

24

record.pages[1].elements[27].text:

what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[13].x:

198

record.pages[2].elements[13].top:

632

record.pages[2].elements[13].width:

184

record.pages[2].elements[13].size:

record.pages[2].elements[14].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.

record.pages[2].elements[26].type:

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee
Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s
preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet
describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to
the same leaflet.

record.pages[2].elements[26].x:

24

record.pages[2].elements[26].top:

273

record.pages[2].elements[26].width:

196

record.pages[2].elements[26].size:

11

record.pages[2].elements[26].color:

111421

record.pages[2].elements[26].max_height:

170

record.pages[2].elements[26].leading:

12.32

record.pages[2].elements[27].id:

management-maintenance-028

record.pages[2].elements[27].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[27].text:

The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools
will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values
an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have
preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently
started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo
- every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned
to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have
expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[18].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

record.editorial_guidance.audience:

People who love games; no technical background assumed.

record.editorial_guidance.rule:

No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.

record.editorial_guidance.keep_internal:

Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README
only.

record.editorial_guidance.qualifications:

Picture captions should describe the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss
development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and
development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea
captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.

record.editorial_guidance.preserve:

Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.

record.editorial_guidance.writing_style:

Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations.
Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

record.editorial_guidance.corporate_horror:

Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not
disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other
fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.

record.editorial_guidance.pending_revision:

Feedback through October 16 incorporated into edition 19; regeneration authorized.

record.editorial_guidance.todos:

Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous
high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small
italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay
is unfinished.

record.editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision:

First description preserved; redundant paragraph and idle inset replaced with Tony horror reaction.

record.pages[1].elements[25].type:

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

24

record.pages[1].elements[27].text:

what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee
Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s
preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet
describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to
the same leaflet.

The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools
will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values
an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have
preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.

legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The service appointment is
unlikely to go as planned.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

para

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently
started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo
- every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned
to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have
expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[18].type:

para

record.pages[4].elements[18].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

### Record: marketing/magazine/guide-assets-v3/provenance.json

Source SHA256: `f200560aa7365bbc256e60c3c280ac72edb5b93849e3cd6f9d1c21fe81d88763`.

record.date:

2026-10-14

record.edition:

3

record.cover.path:

record.cover.tool:

Built-in image_gen

record.cover.prompt:

Use case: ads-marketing. Create original cinematic painted 1990s action game magazine cover ART ONLY, no typography.
Reference 1 Tony identity: spiky dark hair, navy shirt, teal overalls. Reference 2 Sean identity: COMPLETELY BALD
scalp including sides, chin-only beard, NO moustache, orange shirt, blue overalls. Reference 3 Flushfiend monster:
angry ceramic toilet with red eyes, teeth and pipe legs. Reference 4 Hallowed Widow: hairy black spider, white
feather wings, golden halo, red eyes. Portrait composition. Tony and Sean stand together back-to-back as equal
central heroes in a copper-pipe industrial basement, fighting a surrounding HORDE of at least six normal-sized
Flushfiends and four flying Hallowed Widows. Tony fires a compact silver teal pressure gun with brass nozzle
leftward; Sean aims a bulky red-plunger launcher rightward. Clearly visible faces, full heroic bodies, dynamic
diagonal motion, splashing water, atmospheric amber and teal light. Men are unmistakably cooperating, weapons
pointed outward at monsters, never at one another. Monsters encircle sides and foreground but do not obscure heroes.
High-detail realistic painted pulp cover, expressive believable faces matching references, tactile ceramic, fabric,
feathers and metal. No bosses, no giant fatberg, no Clogfather, no AI monster, no portal, no new species. No text,
lettering, watermark or logos. Keep both heroes centrally within the middle 75 percent and all faces below top 15
percent; usable dark atmosphere around edges for magazine design. Exactly two human heroes, normal anatomy.

record.editorial_guidance.audience:

People who love games; no technical background assumed.

record.editorial_guidance.rule:

No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.

record.editorial_guidance.keep_internal:

Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README
only.

record.editorial_guidance.qualifications:

Picture captions should describe the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss
development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and
development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea
captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.

record.editorial_guidance.preserve:

Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.

record.editorial_guidance.writing_style:

Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations.
Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for
repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.

record.editorial_guidance.corporate_horror:

Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not
disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other
fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.

record.editorial_guidance.pending_revision:

Feedback through October 16 incorporated into edition 19; regeneration authorized.

record.editorial_guidance.todos:

Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous
high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small
italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay
is unfinished.

record.editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision:

First description preserved; redundant paragraph and idle inset replaced with Tony horror reaction.

record.editorial_guidance.disclaimers:

Do not add fictional-company, fictional-publication or non-affiliation disclaimers to reader-facing magazine
content.

record.pages[1].elements[25].type:

record.pages[1].elements[25].text:

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building, and keeping essential
systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him
off. A large spider might slow him down a little.

what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.

record.pages[2].elements[13].text:

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution
warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get
their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it
might be unpleasant.

record.pages[2].elements[14].text:

face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.

record.pages[2].elements[26].type:

record.pages[2].elements[26].text:

Mainframe Plumbing &amp; Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee
Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s
preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet
describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to
the same leaflet.

record.pages[2].elements[26].x:

24

record.pages[2].elements[26].top:

273

record.pages[2].elements[26].width:

196

record.pages[2].elements[26].size:

record.pages[2].elements[26].max_height:

170

record.pages[2].elements[26].leading:

record.pages[2].elements[27].id:

management-maintenance-028

record.pages[2].elements[27].type:

para

record.pages[2].elements[27].text:

The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools
will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values
an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have
preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.

unlikely to go as planned.

record.pages[3].elements[23].type:

para

record.pages[3].elements[23].text:

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently
started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo
- every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned
to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have
expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.

record.pages[4].elements[18].type:

para

record.pages[4].elements[18].text:

The Septic Air Force earned its name when a maintenance crew found a swarm circling a blocked vent with the
persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in
close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so
little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a
commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.

record.design_guidance.format:

Eight-page 1990s magazine; grouped features, asymmetric columns, bright banners, bordered pictures, cutout
characters and compact captions.

record.design_guidance.creatures:

Four creatures share a two-page spread. One separate curated action gallery; no complete sheets.

record.design_guidance.references:

User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.

### Record: storybook/curation-backlog.json

Source SHA256: `0e12b8e82d18cd471787483d5dfe59bfe2c540562b39928020383aa91fc926ee`.

record.status:

Editorial curation plan; no capture permission granted

record.reviewed_through:

055

record.ownership:

Storyboarding curates prose and book structure; Engineering preserves builds and supplies verified delivery
facts/captures. Coordinate before editing shared README/HTML.

record.editorial_practice[0]:

Preserve every earlier chapter, original image, and versioned design.

record.editorial_practice[1]:

Retain funny failures and rejected directions with reason and date; do not invent anecdotes.

record.editorial_practice[2]:

Track character, menu, enemy, environment and audio evolution with before/after pairs.

record.editorial_practice[3]:

Label each image gameplay capture, concept, mockup, or asset preview.

record.editorial_practice[4]:

Later captures of archived builds must record capture date separately from original build date.

record.editorial_practice[5]:

A current build screenshot cannot fill an older chapter’s capture gap.

record.editorial_practice[6]:

Keep extra usable images in chapter folders even if only a selection is embedded.

record.capture_priorities[0]:

Earliest existing captures as baseline; retain originals.

record.capture_priorities[1]:

Selection evolution: original cards, clipboard, punch clock and employee photo treatments.

record.capture_priorities[2]:

BJ server rack and semantic portraits; before/after dialogue presentation.

record.capture_priorities[3]:

Full route versus faster opening and continuous encounters; wastewater progression.

record.capture_priorities[4]:

Tape checkpoint versus dispenser, then glass cabinet and one-spare revision.

record.capture_priorities[5]:

Widow/swarm evolution and readable damage/debris.

record.capture_priorities[6]:

Latest title/gameplay with version badge; app icon system preview separately labeled.

record.prompts[0].text:

Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: premium hyperrealistic fictional videogame weapon product portrait for GLOBAL
PLUMBING INITIATIVE. Single isolated tool, no person, no hands, no duplicate tool. Square composition, 2048x2048
desired. Entire tool fully visible with generous 12 percent margins, diagonal orientation lower-left handle to
upper-right working end, slightly elevated three-quarter camera, centered on a dark charcoal-blue workshop display
surface with a soft contact shadow. Defocused copper pipe shapes far behind, no clutter. Consistent cinematic studio
lighting across the set: broad cool teal rim light from rear left, warm amber key light from upper right, neutral
realistic material colors. Finely detailed machined steel, worn painted enamel, rubber texture, subtle service wear,
restrained condensation. Photoreal practical movie prop, plausible exterior materials but whimsical plumbing
action-game design, not a modern military gun. Premium catalog photography, 85mm lens appearance, crisp whole-tool
focus, shallow background depth of field. No typography, brand logo, watermark, technical dimensions, diagrams,
cutaways, exposed internal machinery, extra accessories or firing effects. One hero product only. Subject: Sean's
oversized manual two-handed demolition HAMMER, a huge solid rectangular forged-steel sledge head with blunt flat
faces, substantial long dark steel handle and bright orange ribbed rubber grip. Comically overbuilt heavy impact
tool for a weighty overhead slam, never a powered jackhammer. Massive readable steel head, orange lower grip, bolted
orange collar at head. A clumsy apprentice's brute-force tool. No spikes, no blades, no gore.

Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: premium hyperrealistic fictional videogame weapon product portrait for GLOBAL
PLUMBING INITIATIVE. Single isolated tool, no person, no hands, no duplicate tool. Square composition, 2048x2048
desired. Entire tool fully visible with generous 12 percent margins, diagonal orientation lower-left handle to
upper-right working end, slightly elevated three-quarter camera, centered on a dark charcoal-blue workshop display
surface with a soft contact shadow. Defocused copper pipe shapes far behind, no clutter. Consistent cinematic studio
lighting across the set: broad cool teal rim light from rear left, warm amber key light from upper right, neutral
realistic material colors. Finely detailed machined steel, worn painted enamel, rubber texture, subtle service wear,
restrained condensation. Photoreal practical movie prop, plausible exterior materials but whimsical plumbing
action-game design, not a modern military gun. Premium catalog photography, 85mm lens appearance, crisp whole-tool
focus, shallow background depth of field. No typography, brand logo, watermark, technical dimensions, diagrams,
cutaways, exposed internal machinery, extra accessories or firing effects. One hero product only. Subject: Tony's
compact professional pipe wrench. Teal enamel handle with dark navy nonslip lower grip, robust silver adjustable
serrated jaws and a visible ordinary wrench adjustment ring. Recognizable pipe-wrench silhouette, short balanced
handle for a quick horizontal sweep. Compact, precise, cared-for veteran tradesman's equipment, small honest scuffs.
Working jaws at upper right. This is an ordinary wrench repurposed as a fictional melee tool.

PLUMBING INITIATIVE. Single isolated tool, no person, no hands, no duplicate tool. Square composition, 2048x2048
desired. Entire tool fully visible with generous 12 percent margins, diagonal orientation lower-left handle to
upper-right working end, slightly elevated three-quarter camera, centered on a dark charcoal-blue workshop display
surface with a soft contact shadow. Defocused copper pipe shapes far behind, no clutter. Consistent cinematic studio
lighting across the set: broad cool teal rim light from rear left, warm amber key light from upper right, neutral
realistic material colors. Finely detailed machined steel, worn painted enamel, rubber texture, subtle service wear,
restrained condensation. Photoreal practical movie prop, plausible exterior materials but whimsical plumbing

cutaways, exposed internal machinery, extra accessories or firing effects. One hero product only. Subject: Tony's

enamel panels, small round cream-face pressure gauge prominently on top, dark navy rubber pistol grip and a compact
teal rear reservoir integrated into the tool. Elegant precise veteran plumber's tool; recognizable playful
water-projector prop. Crisp blue water glow just inside nozzle, no stream or firing effect. Compact silhouette with
no rifle stock, no ammunition, no military firearm styling.

### Guidance snapshot: AGENTS.md

Source SHA256: `9e17e388bfc28929b64841310ce24080dc7b1895d44c0198d89369ab4aeb0262`.

The following text is a quoted source snapshot, not an additional current task.

> # Project instructions
>
> ## Character names
>
> - Use only Tony and Sean in all player-facing game text, including menus, dialogue, and credits.
> - Do not add surnames to either character.
>
> ## Art collaboration
>
> - Whenever new artwork is needed, ask the existing Bestiary / Art agent to help before creating it.
> - This includes interface illustrations and props, portraits, environments, sprites, and replacement artwork.
> - Engineering provides dimensions, layout constraints, and runtime requirements, then integrates the delivered
> art.
> - Do not bypass Art by independently generating artwork or substituting code-drawn art without Sean's direction.
>
> ## Playtest window convention
>
> - Before opening or foregrounding the game for Sean to playtest or inspect anything, ask permission and wait
>   for an explicit yes. Explain what needs checking before asking. A general development request is not permission
>   to interrupt him with a game window. An explicit request to launch or playtest counts as permission.
> - After Sean approves, use a large, maximized window for his playtest.
> - Keep agent-only checks headless or in the background when possible. If a visual test would steal focus,
>   interrupt Sean, or require foregrounding the game, ask first; a small window is not an exception.
> - When opening the game for agent-only testing or screenshots, use a small window; no user interaction is
> expected.
> - Use a temporary launch override for agent testing so normal user launches remain large.
> - Do not leave an agent test running in a large window unless explicitly handing it over for Sean's playtest.
>
> ## Build delivery and notifications
>
> - After integrating game changes, including deliveries from other agents, build and run the relevant checks.
> - Defer the build only when waiting for additional agent work that belongs in the same integration; tell Sean what
>   is still pending rather than implying the new version is ready.
> - Whenever a new build is ready, proactively tell Sean its version, what changed, and any remaining testing gaps.
> - If a build fails, report the failure and do not describe it as ready to play.
> - Building does not authorize opening or foregrounding the game; keep the playtest permission rules above.
>
> ## Roadmap maintenance
>
> - Keep `roadmap.html` current whenever work is added, completed, changed, deferred, or reprioritized.
> - Update affected descriptions, milestone order, statuses, remaining work, and current build/date as applicable.
> - Make these updates in the same delivery as the work; do not wait for a separate user reminder.
> - Distinguish partial progress from completed milestones and proposed ideas from agreed plans.
> - Keep roadmap claims aligned with the running build and the development storybook.
>
> ## Development storybook
>
> The user wants screenshots of every iteration to tell the story of the game's graphics and capabilities.
>
> - For each delivered game iteration, capture actual screenshots of the running build before replacing it.
> - Save original PNG or JPEG captures in `storybook/NNN-short-title/`, using the next three-digit iteration number.
> - Keep earlier captures and entries intact; never overwrite an earlier iteration with newer artwork.
> - Include a representative gameplay view and additional views when needed to show a new feature or milestone.
> - Append a dated entry to `storybook/README.md` with embedded screenshots, a short narrative, new capabilities,
>   and what is still placeholder or incomplete. Use the user's America/Los_Angeles date.
> - Record the game version and, when available, the source commit or build identifier.
> - Capture only the game window, avoiding unrelated desktop content. Use the approved computer-use screenshot tool.
> - Keep the storybook in the project, outside ignored build/scratch folders, and exclude it from Godot game
> imports.
> - If capture is blocked, record the gap honestly and preserve the build for later capture; do not fabricate
> screenshots.
>
> ### Making-of book curation
>
> - Storyboarding owns ongoing editorial curation of the development storybook, coordinating with Engineering.
> - Collect generous early, middle, and late development material for an eventual making-of book: milestone
>   screenshots, before/after comparisons, character/menu/environment evolution, funny failures, and design pivots.
> - Preserve earlier chapters and originals. Label concept art, rejected ideas, and actual gameplay captures
> distinctly.
> - Engineering preserves builds and supplies actual screenshots under the existing permission rules. This standing
>   collection request does not authorize opening or foregrounding the game without permission.
> - Maintain a capture backlog for missing milestones so they can be photographed during an approved session.
> - Timestamp every new storybook capture and making-of artifact with `YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS` in the filename and
>   its entry/metadata, using `America/Los_Angeles` (for example, `20261016-233045-title-screen.png`).
> - Record the timezone and UTC offset in metadata to disambiguate daylight-saving transitions. Distinguish actual
>   capture/creation time from later archival/import time; add a suffix if filenames would collide within one
> second.
> - Preserve historical originals. Backfill exact timestamps only from trustworthy capture records; retain known
>   dates and mark exact times unknown when unavailable. File copy/modification time is not proof of capture time.
>
> ## Bestiary maintenance
>
> - Keep `bestiary/bestiary.html` current when adding or revising a monster, its artwork, or implementation status.
> - Give every creature a name, description, one gallery portrait, and links to game sprites and animation
> information.
> - Maintain separate pixel-art game sprites and hyperrealistic marketing portraits for each creature.
> - Store marketing portraits in `bestiary/<creature>/` with versioned filenames and preserve exact generation
> prompts.
> - Name creature folders after the monster using lowercase hyphenated names. Each contains `monster.json`.
> - Treat `monster.json` as the source for names, descriptions, and backstories; synchronize the gallery and
> catalog.
> - Keep stable creature IDs when renaming. Metadata asset paths are relative to the project root.
> - Leave backstory text empty with status `pending` until the storyboarding agent supplies it.
> - Preserve earlier artwork. Keep `assets/bestiary/catalog.json` aligned with the gallery and current asset paths.
> - Distinguish animation source artwork from validated runtime animations and playable enemies from planned
> creatures.
> - Keep marketing assets excluded from Godot imports with `bestiary/.gdignore`; record actual image dimensions.
>
> ## Makefile conventions
>
> Read [.github/instructions/makefile.instructions.md](.github/instructions/makefile.instructions.md)
> before creating or editing Makefiles. These reusable conventions were brought over from Kandra:
> self-documenting default help, source-order sections, orange headers, white target names, real tabs,
> inline descriptions, and emoji progress. Preserve the Godot toolchain used by this game.
>
> ## Combat metadata maintenance
>
> - Give every new monster a `health` object in its `monster.json`, including positive maximum and spawn HP,
>   progression placement, health-bar visibility, balance rationale, and weapon hit-count comparisons.
> - Follow `assets/bestiary/balance-policy.json`; compare both plumbers' available exclusive weapons.
> - Mirror health summaries in `assets/bestiary/catalog.json` and the gallery. Keep design and runtime values
> distinct.
> - Keep weapon mechanics in `weapons/<weapon-id>/weapon.json` and register each weapon in `weapons/catalog.json`.
> - Bestiary owns each weapon's `game-art.json`; Marketing owns its `marketing-art.json`. Preserve versioned
> originals,
>   exact generation prompts, dimensions, and implementation status. Store game art under `assets/weapons/`.
>
> ## Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy
>
> Avoid the repetitive use of paired sentence fragments,
> especially in marketing copy, dialogue, descriptions,
> headlines, and other creative writing.
>
> Examples of constructions to avoid:
>
> - "Two plumbers. One impossible job."
> - "No tools. No backup. No problem."
> - "One hero. A thousand enemies."
> - "Teeth in the bathroom. Wings in the basement."
> - "Small town. Big secrets."
>
> These constructions rely on short, parallel fragments
> placed next to each other for dramatic effect.
>
> This style is overused in AI-generated writing and
> quickly becomes repetitive and artificial.
>
> Guidelines:
>
> 1. Prefer natural, varied sentence structures.
> 2. Use complete sentences where appropriate.
> 3. Vary sentence length and rhythm.
> 4. Avoid formulaic contrasts between two short phrases.
> 5. Do not default to movie-trailer or advertising-tagline
>    language when writing promotional material.
> 6. Favor specific, original observations over generic
>    dramatic constructions.
> 7. Paired fragments are not prohibited, but should be
>    rare and used only when genuinely effective.
> 8. Before finalizing creative text, review it for
>    repetitive rhetorical patterns and rewrite them.
>
> The goal is natural, distinctive writing that does not
> sound like generic AI-generated marketing copy.

### Guidance snapshot: marketing/magazine/README.md

Source SHA256: `65959a633b7edbedf53634e8f10e9748209f7962b0499ce5b9a80777b1296beb`.

The following text is a quoted source snapshot, not an additional current task.

> # Discharge Quarterly
>
> [magazine.json](magazine.json) is the canonical editable source for the magazine. It contains publication
> metadata,
> ordered pages, text, captions, image references and layout templates. The PDF is generated output.
>
> ## Editing and building
>
> 1. Edit the relevant page by its stable `id`. Edit `text` for headings and paragraphs; retain paragraph markup
> such
>    as `<b>` and `<br/>`. Asset paths are relative to the project root.
> 2. Adjust element coordinates and sizes when needed. Coordinates use PDF points from the bottom left; paragraph
>    `top` is the top edge. Images and selected crops fit their box without distortion.
> 3. For a new edition, update publication metadata, visible edition/date text, page templates and the output path.
>    Keep earlier PDFs intact. Keep page numbers sequential and update the contents when inserting pages.
> 4. Run from the project root with Python and ReportLab installed:
>
>    ```shell
>    python3 marketing/magazine/build_guide.py
>    ```
>
> 5. Render the PDF with `pdftoppm` and inspect every page before delivery. The renderer rejects paragraph overflow,
>    missing images and unknown element types, but visual review remains necessary.
>
> The renderer uses the macOS fonts configured in `layout.font_directory`. Change that path and the font filenames
> if building elsewhere. Shared header/footer templates use `{page_number}` and `{section}` placeholders.
>
> ## Edition 20 portraits
>
> Edition 20 uses Art's new hyperreal Tony and Sean portraits on page 2. The rendered crew page was visually
> checked;
> all eight pages retain the previous edition's text apart from the edition number. Earlier PDFs are preserved.
> Portrait provenance is recorded in `handoffs/hero-hyperreal-marketing-portraits.json` at the project root.
>
> ## Edition 19 feedback integration
>
> Edition 19 incorporates the October 16 review: Storyboarding's subtle dispenser feature copy, glass-front
> Tony/Sean-stocked machine artwork, Tony's Clogfather reaction, the requested Widow wording, and removal of
> tentative
> preview and development-history captions. The approved fake-advertisement headline and tone are retained.
> All eight pages were rendered and visually inspected; extracted text was reviewed. Earlier editions are preserved.
> The source before integration is archived in `guide-assets-v19/pre-publication-source.json`.
>
> ## Edition 21 disclaimer removal
>
> Removed the fictional-company footer and fictional-publication/non-affiliation paragraph. All eight pages rendered
> and visually checked; extracted text audited. `current.pdf` matches edition 21.
>
> ## Editorial policy
>
> Do not include fictional-company, fictional-publication or non-affiliation disclaimers in the reader edition.
>
> Suggest the dispenser's disturbing corporate practices through euphemisms and omissions. Do not describe its
> lethal mechanism or bodily processing. Never mention the viewer's screen or other fourth-wall-breaking details.
>
> Write for people who love games. Assume no knowledge of game design or development. This rule applies to the
> cover, contents, profiles, headings, captions, sidebars, credits and PDF metadata, not just body paragraphs.
> Describe what readers can see or experience. Player terms such as health, attacks, checkpoint and reload are fine.
>
> Keep sprite-sheet terminology, atlas details, frame counts, build IDs, runtime/integration status, collision
> rules,
> validation notes and agent/process commentary out of the publication. Do not disguise technical explanations with
> new headings: remove row/column/frame-count descriptions. Keep technical records in internal manifests and this
> README. The `editorial_guidance` object in the JSON is internal guidance and is not rendered.
>
> Remove tentative captions such as “Preview artwork,” “An idea we're exploring,” and “This account is still
> taking shape.” Keep production status and image provenance in internal records. Picture captions should describe
> the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss earlier versions, development
> history,
> prototype status or production progress in the magazine. Never imply unfinished encounters are playable.
>
> Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must use `TODO: <specific missing item>` in a conspicuous high-contrast
> box with bold type at least 18 pt. Allow enough space to prevent clipping. Never hide TODOs in small italic
> captions
> or vague caveats. Existing artwork does not need a TODO merely because gameplay remains unfinished.
>
> Keep future plot spoilers, creature-origin explanations and boss solutions out of promotional copy. Preserve
> approved profiles and lore, current names, and honest qualifications for unsettled stories. Preserve historical
> screenshots and earlier editions. Request new illustrations through Bestiary / Art. Do not change mechanics or
> canonical creature records while editing the magazine.
>
> Extract the complete PDF text and audit it for development jargon, including bookmarks and metadata. Render and
> visually inspect every affected page after rewriting; check that shorter copy still fits the layout naturally.
>
> Follow the writing-style guidance in `../../AGENTS.md`. Prefer natural, varied sentences and specific observations
> rather than repeated paired fragments or generic dramatic contrasts. Review headings, captions and body copy for
> repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.
>
> ## Edition 18 editorial revision
>
> Edition 18 retains the eight-page design and revises repetitive headlines, captions and promotional copy.
> Approved character and creature lore remains intact. The complete extracted text was reviewed and all eight
> rendered pages were visually checked. Edition 17's source is archived in `guide-assets-v18/`.
>
> ## Edition 17 layout direction
>
> Use the supplied 1990s Nintendo Power and GamePro spreads as the visual reference: large shadowed display type,
> bright section banners, compact columns, small bordered pictures, cutout characters and conversational captions.
> Vary the page composition by feature. Avoid returning to one large portrait and several pages per creature.
>
> The eight-page issue contains a cover, paired crew profiles, BJ and dispenser half-page features, a two-page
> creature roundup, a gameplay feature, one curated action gallery and an in-universe back-cover advertisement.
> Keep full animation sheets out of the reader edition. Select a few complete poses for the action gallery and
> inspect the crops against their actual artwork boundaries. Preserve proportions and original files.
>
> All layout elements and text remain in `magazine.json`. Display text supports `angle`, `outline` and
> `stroke_width`; paragraphs support an optional `font`. Font choices remain in the JSON layout settings.
>
> ## Automatic web publication
>
> The PDF generator also refreshes `current.pdf`, the stable Git LFS publication file. After visual review, commit
> and push that file to `main`. The **Publish magazine** GitHub Actions workflow renders its pages and deploys
> only the reader, page images, and downloadable PDF to GitHub Pages. Local generation alone does not publish.
>
> The HTML reader reproduces the PDF pages as images rather than reflowing the design. It includes page navigation
> and the original PDF for selectable text and full-resolution zoom. Image-only pages are not a screen-reader
> replacement for the document. GitHub Actions uses the finished PDF, so macOS fonts are not needed on the server.
>
> Expected address: [Discharge Quarterly](https://jugglingbear.github.io/drain-damage/).
> The workflow can also be rerun manually from GitHub Actions. Failed builds leave the previous deployment intact.
>
> To preview the generated site locally with Poppler installed:
>
> ```sh
> python3 tools/build_magazine_site.py
> python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory builds/magazine-site
> ```
>
> Open `http://localhost:8000` in a browser. Generated site files stay in the ignored builds folder.
